historical_growth.revenue_note: FY2023 65,322 -> FY2026 73,712 (53wk) = 4.1%; FY2021 57,887 -> FY2026 = 5.0%. On the 52-week equivalent (72,464) the figures are 3.5% and 4.6%. Growth is mostly food inflation plus ~1pp share gain; underlying LFL FY26 was 3.5%.
historical_growth.eps_note: Statutory diluted EPS is distorted at both ends: FY2023 (9.9p) carried large impairments and FY2021 (61.7p) the £5bn Asia disposal gain, so neither CAGR is meaningful. Adjusted diluted EPS: FY2023 21.9p -> FY2026 29.0p (52wk) = ~9.9% 3yr CAGR, roughly 3% profit growth plus ~5%/yr share-count reduction from buybacks.
historical_growth.equity_note: Book equity shrinks because buybacks + dividends (£2.4bn FY26) exceed net income (£1.8bn); equity CAGR is not a usable growth proxy for a capital-returning grocer.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal): FY2022 1,871; FY2023 1,680; FY2024 1,431; FY2025 391 (1,299 ex the £908m Bank deposit repayment); FY2026 1,199. 3yr CAGR FY2023->FY2026 = -10.6%, driven by cash tax rising from an abnormally low £123m (FY23) to £503m (FY26) and by stripping interest income that grew from £87m to £233m. The 5yr figure is undefined: FY2021 owner FCF was -£1,480m after the £2,851m one-off pension contribution. SBC is flat at ~0.2% of revenue, so SBC growth is not the cause. Reported FCF 3yr CAGR was -3.2%.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr on a 52-week basis (3.5%) tempered to ~3% for the forward base path: FY26 LFL 3.5% with food inflation easing, FY27 adj. operating profit guided flat-to-up (£3.0-3.3bn vs £3,152m), medium-term FCF guidance £1.5-2.0bn.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-1% to -2%) diverges from revenue (4-5%) and adjusted EPS (~10%) by more than 30%: book value is being shrunk deliberately by buybacks and dividends, so the equity series is not used.

scenario_narratives.base: Steady defensive compounder: ~3% nominal sales growth fading to 2%, adjusted operating margin flat at ~4.2-4.3% with Save to Invest and retail media offsetting UK cost headwinds, capex ~2.1-2.2% of sales, cash tax normalising to 27%. The price-investment flywheel keeps share at ~28.5% but does not expand margin.
scenario_narratives.bull: Share-gain flywheel plus capital-light mix shift: retail media/dunnhumby, Marketplace and IMS lift margin ~50bps over five years, FY27 at the top of guidance, sales growth 3-3.75%, lease intensity falling as owned-estate share rises. Terminal 2.5% growth at 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Price war meets cost shock: Aldi/Lidl/Asda pressure plus business rates, EPR, NI and an energy/food cost spike compress margin ~60bps permanently, growth slows to 1.5-2%, capex and lease costs rise. A de-rating, not a solvency event. Terminal 1.5% at 15x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Tesco is valued as an unlevered owner-FCF stream after the full cost of its leases (treatment B), with SBC expensed and the share count held flat. The business is a defensive, low-growth, low-margin compounder whose value is dominated by the terminal multiple rather than growth; the stock trades near its 52-week high at ~17x adjusted EPS and ~17x its own levered FCF, which the house basis only supports on the bull-leaning end of the scenario range. The buyback is value-neutral in this frame: it changes EPS, not the owner's share of a fixed cash stream.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal multiple dominates: at 2% growth and 7.5% WACC the cap/Gordon choice (15-20x) moves value by ~15%; a UK grocer re-rating to 12-13x FCF would put the price above every scenario.
Margin: each 10bps of adjusted operating margin is ~£75m of EBIT, ~£55m of FCF and ~10-12p/share; business rates reform, EPR and NI are unmodelled beyond the guidance year except via the bear path.

Lease treatment: treatment B charges the full £1.06bn lease payment in perpetuity; treatment A (leases as debt, £7.9bn) would give a similar value only if ROU renewal capex is charged - switching treatments without that adjustment moves value by ~£1/share either way.
Stale anchors: net debt and share count are from 28 Feb 2026; ~7 months of buybacks (~£800m, ~160m shares) and the H1 FY27 balance sheet are not yet reflected.
Cash tax: full-expensing capital allowances keep cash tax ~£200m below the P&L charge; the model ramps to 27% so any permanence of the gap is upside, any reversal (timing catch-up) is downside.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 411.7-516.2 GBp.
data_sources.financials: research/TSCO.L/Reports/TSCO.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2017-FY2026 annuals and H1s) and TSCO.L_Annual_FY2026.txt (53 weeks to 28 Feb 2026): cash flow statement, Note 9 EPS, Note 13 Leases, Note 22 Borrowings, Note 29 Share capital, Note 30 Own shares, APM free-cash-flow reconciliation.
data_sources.qualitative: research/TSCO.L/Reports/TSCO.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): FY26 results and FY27 guidance (adj. OP £3.0-3.3bn, capex c.£1.6bn, tax c.27%, medium-term FCF £1.5-2.0bn), competitive position, risks.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025/26 statutory revenue inc. fuel, 53 weeks to 28 Feb 2026 (52-week equivalent £72,464m). Year-1 growth below embeds the ~1.7% reversal of the 53rd week.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 28 Feb 2026: 6,385m called-up shares (Note 29) less 36.4m held by employee benefit trusts = 6,349m basic, plus 99m potentially dilutive awards (Note 9 diluted EPS table) = 6,448m. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. The ongoing buyback (£1,443m / 351.7m shares in FY26, ~5.5% of capital) is value-neutral in this model: it is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and the rest of it is already captured as distributable owner FCF. No post-Feb-2026 buybacks are reflected; refresh the count when the H1 FY27 interim (early Oct 2026) is extracted.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt BEFORE lease liabilities, Tesco APM at 28 Feb 2026 (£2,679m; FY25 £1,738m): borrowings £7,196m less cash £2,515m, short-term investments £1,429m and net derivatives/JV loans. Lease liabilities (£7,884m) are deliberately EXCLUDED because the full lease payment is charged inside the flows (treatment B). Headline Tesco net debt incl. leases is £10,563m.
inputs.cash_note: £2,515m cash and equivalents + £1,429m short-term investments at 28 Feb 2026.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Levered owner FCF FY26 = reported FCF 2,240 - SBC 140 - interest income 233 - lease principal 668 = 1,199. Reported OCF is already after interest paid (£759m incl. £395m lease interest) and tax paid (£503m). The engine's projections are UNLEVERED (EBITDA -> lease cost -> D&A -> cash tax -> capex -> WC), so year-1 projected FCF (~£1.7bn) sits above this figure by after-tax net non-lease interest (~£90m) plus the FY26 one-offs removed; Tesco's own 'Free cash flow' APM was £1,957m (52wk) and includes the £233m one-off interest income on Bank proceeds, £52m dividends received and a £385m working-capital inflow.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF £3,906m less capex £1,666m (statutory capex incl. property buybacks), 53 weeks. FY2020 (£38m OCF, Bank), FY2021 (£2,851m one-off pension payment) and FY2025 (£908m Bank deposit repayment on divestiture) are distorted years and were not used as a base.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, Group cash flow statement share-based payments add-back £140m (FY25 £136m); no separate equity-award tax line in the UK filings (EquityAwardTaxes 0). Own shares purchased for schemes (£100m) is the cash settlement of the same awards and is not charged again.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income £233m FY26 stripped from the owner-FCF base: it is largely interest on the c.£700m Tesco Bank sale proceeds (since returned via buybacks) and on cash that is netted inside the net-debt bridge. Management guides net finance costs to normalise upward as this tailwind fades.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). Per-share values are computed in GBP and multiplied by 100 to pence; fx_rate 100 is a fixed definitional conversion, not a market rate, so it cannot go stale. Parity check: adjusted diluted EPS 29.0p x ~17.4x = 503.8p quote, consistent with a GBP->pence conversion of x100.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the flows' currency. 10y gilt ~4.5%, UK ERP 5.0%, beta 0.65-0.75 for a defensive UK grocer -> cost of equity ~7.75-8.25%. Weighted-average rate on senior unsecured debt 4.0% (Note 22), after 25% tax ~3.0%. Market cap ~£32.5bn vs net financial debt £2.7bn (leases excluded under treatment B) -> ~8% debt weight. WACC = 7.5%, used identically in all three scenarios; cyclicality and competitive risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) - leases as operating cost. The full IFRS 16 lease cash payment (FY26: principal £668m + interest £395m = £1,063m, 1.44% of revenue) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (£7,884m) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (total D&A £1,895m - ROU depreciation £591m per Note 13 = £1,304m, 1.77% of revenue). Check: pre-IFRS16 EBIT = adj. operating profit 3,194 + ROU dep 591 - lease cash 1,063 = 2,722, which ties to the FY0 component build (EBITDA 7.09% - SBC 0.19% - lease 1.44% - D&A 1.77% of 73,712 = 2,722).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are nil/immaterial at FY26 (NCI share of profit £0m; FY25 £4m). No deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, probability-weighted, 10-year horizon. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: Tesco is a standard operating company (UK grocery retail + Booker wholesale + Central Europe + small IMS insurance/money-services arm, ~0.3% of revenue after the Nov-2024 sale of Tesco Bank to Barclays), so the owner-FCF route applies with the non-US adaptations (GBP WACC, lease treatment B, GBp quote). EBITDA margin in the drivers is ADJUSTED EBITDA BEFORE SBC (adj. operating profit 3,194 + D&A 1,895 + SBC 140 = 5,229, 7.09% on 53 weeks) so the engine's SBC deduction does not double-charge. Cash tax is modelled below the 26.8% adjusted P&L rate initially (FY26 cash tax £503m vs £712m P&L charge, full-expensing capital allowances; deferred tax on accelerated capital allowances grew £119m) and ramps to 27% by year 5. Working capital: grocer with structurally negative working capital (payables > inventory + receivables), so growth releases cash; captured at a modest 4% of the revenue change in base (FY26 inflow £385m, FY25 outflow £45m). Buyback is value-neutral here (see share_count_basis); Tesco IS funding the flat count (£1,443m repurchased FY26 vs £140m SBC). The £220m pension surplus and the c.£0.7bn surplus of property market value over book are NOT added to the bridge (not realisable without ceasing to trade from the stores). SBC-light market: house/street band is narrow (SBC 0.19% of revenue) but not zero. H1 FY2026/27 interim results (early Oct 2026) are not in the Extracted folder: price is live but net debt and share count are the 28 Feb 2026 annual figures and should be refreshed when the interim is extracted.

bear.narrative: A renewed UK price war (Asda's reset, Aldi/Lidl expansion) forces deeper price investment just as business rates reform, the EPR levy, NI and wage inflation land, and the Middle East-driven energy/food cost shock management cited when widening FY27 guidance pushes profit to the bottom of £3.0-3.3bn and then lower: adjusted operating margin erodes to ~3.6-3.7% and stays there. Sales growth slows to 1.5-2% as volume share stalls; capex intensity rises to defend the estate and lease costs drift up with indexation. No solvency issue - net financial debt is £2.7bn against £5bn EBITDA - so this is a margin and multiple de-rating case, not a distress case. Terminal growth 1.5%, cap 15x.

base.growth_note: Y1 = ~+3.2% underlying less ~1.7% 53rd-week reversal. Thereafter food-inflation-plus-share-gain nominal growth fading to 2%.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA before SBC. FY26 7.09% (53wk). Y1 7.0% = FY27 guidance midpoint £3.15bn adj. OP + D&A ~£1.95bn + SBC on £74.8bn. Save to Invest (~£500m/yr) and retail media offset business rates, EPR levy, NI and price investment; no net margin expansion assumed beyond +10bps.
base.capex_note: FY27 guidance c.£1.6bn ongoing capex (2.14% of Y1 revenue) plus ~£50-100m of property buybacks; FY26 statutory capex £1,666m (2.26%).
base.terminal_note: Cap at 18x terminal FCF (not the 20x default): mature, defensive, ~2% growth. Gordon at 7.5%/2.0% implies 18.5x, so the cap binds marginally; the market currently pays ~16.6x Tesco's own (levered) FCF.
base.narrative: Tesco keeps its ~28.5% UK share with LFL growth of ~3% fading to 2% as food inflation normalises; adjusted operating margin holds ~4.2-4.3% because Save to Invest and retail media (dunnhumby / Tesco Media & Insight) absorb business rates reform, the EPR levy and continued Aldi Price Match investment. Capex ~2.1-2.2% of sales, cash tax ramping from 25% to 27%, working capital a small inflow. Owner FCF (unlevered, after full lease cost) runs ~£1.7bn rising to ~£2.2bn by year 10.

bull.narrative: Share gains compound (UK share toward 30%, online share rising with Whoosh), Booker and Central Europe grow mid-single digits, and the capital-light streams (retail media, dunnhumby, Marketplace, IMS) lift adjusted operating margin toward 4.6-4.7% by year 5 while Save to Invest keeps the cost base flat. FY27 lands at the top of the £3.0-3.3bn range; business rates and EPR are absorbed. Owned property (c.60% of space) keeps lease cost drifting down. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 20x.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: management itself widened the FY27 range for geopolitical/cost uncertainty, UK grocery is structurally low-margin with seven competitors above 5% share, and business rates/EPR/NI are hard-coded cost increases. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (continued share gains, retail-media margin lift, and full absorption of the cost headwinds) in a market where margin expansion has historically been competed away. No going-concern or covenant risk, so the bear weight does not go higher.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
